comment: The shapes no other clean fixture reached, pinned so the F6 spec->fixture coverage claim is real: case_expression/case_alternative, lambda_expression, guard_equation, where_block, list_comprehension, qualified_identifier, record_definition/record_field and the class trio. Two contract pins beyond coverage: a qualified call keeps its module qualification (`M.lookupOne`, the Erlang gen_server:cast precedent) and a constructor in a function HEAD pattern is never an `instantiates` — pattern territory is everything before the body FIELD, which is the live form of a gate that used to test for an `operator` child with text `=` (this grammar never produces one, so the gate could not fire). THREE PINS CHANGED in the M14.0 clean-completeness round, each because the old pin was measuring a defect rather than a contract: (1) a where-local now PUBLISHES a symbol, owned by its enclosing frame, carrying its signature's types — measured over the corpus, 1,821 where/with/let binders held 1,361 function definitions and 449 local signatures that published nothing, and 4,107 applications inside where blocks lost their attribution frame entirely; the haskell lane already solved this construct with scoped local identity and Clean did not. `nonNegative` is still NOT exported, so M11.11's export-surface exclusion is unchanged. (2) `uses` is now emitted for a record field, because a record literal and a record update are real uses of a field and this file declares `x` and `y`; the old `forbid uses` pinned the absence of an edge kind, not the absence of a false positive, and the honest pin is the FP one: only a field THIS FILE declares produces an edge. (3) the `qualified_identifier` named in the header comment is CORPUS-DEAD — measured over the 320-file universe it occurs exactly twice and both sites are this repository's own fixtures; the form real Clean code uses is `single_quoted_name` (`'Data.Map'.get`, 233 corpus sites), which is now handled too, so the alias form here is kept as the fixture for the 2-site form and `single-quoted-names.icl` is the fixture for the 233-site form.

It used to be named `Point`, which made this file declare `Point` twice — the type AND the implementation — and that is the phantom-declaration class this round removed: 699 containers on the 312-file population, 1,009 of 6,856 residual edges reachable by deleting them.

expectSymbols.name: nonNegative
expectSymbols.comment: CHANGED: a where-local IS published. It is owned by the frame that encloses it (`describe`), marked visibility `local`, carries the types of the signature written directly above it (`ret=String`, `params=1` for `k`), and is NOT exported. The identity that distinguishes it from a module-level `nonNegative` is its `qualifiedName` (`describe.nonNegative`), which is what the store resolves relationship endpoints against.

forbidExports.name: Point::instance
forbidExports.comment: an implementation is not part of a module's surface. This is also the mechanism-side half of the export fix: `impl` is not an EXPORTABLE kind, so the container cannot be exported even though its ownerName is the module.

expectRelationships.comment: M59.O2 / formula §8: the edge names its site — the `instance Shape Point where` line, on the class NAME node
qualified target keeps its module qualification AND the call site line

CHANGED: the guard equation `| otherwise = nonNegative n` calls the where-local, and the call resolves to the local's SCOPED identity. The old analyzer attributed nothing for it: the whole where block set `currentFunction = undefined`, so this site produced no edge at all.
CHANGED: the frame owns its local, on the local's own naming line

CHANGED: `{ x = px, y = py }` is a record CONSTRUCTION and every field it sets is a use of that field. `x` is declared by this file, so the edge is emitted; a field name this file does not declare produces none (the FP pin below).
CHANGED: `{ p & x = p.x + dx }` is a record UPDATE; the field name is read from the `update_field` node, not by zipping the parallel `field`/`value` field lists

CHANGED: the declared-type reference graph. `makePoint :: !Int !Int -> Point` references `Point` in its result and `Int` twice in its domain; each edge carries the NAME's own line, not the signature's start.
a record FIELD's declared type is a reference from the field
record fields are contained by their type, on the child's own naming line (#921 — the store resolves with this line)
CHANGED: a whole-module import emits the `<module>:*` edge the resolver documents as legitimately unresolved (a namespace has no single target symbol). The per-NAME edges are the ones that resolve.

CHANGED: an `exports` edge per exported name, on the symbol's own line. Clean has no export keyword — a `.dcl`'s definition list IS the interface — so the export surface is a first-class edge rather than a property only the exports array carries.

the TYPE at its definition line. CHANGED FROM 31, WHICH WAS A DEFECT IN THIS PIN AND NOT IN THE ANALYZER: the type has always been contained at L19 and both entries of this pair said 31, so both were satisfied by the container's single edge — the `expectRelationshipCount equals 2` beside them was the only thing keeping the per-site rule honest, and the pair could not tell 2 sites from 1. The container is a different name now, which is what exposed it.
…and the INSTANCE container at ITS line: PER-SITE, two edges at two lines (a per-set implementation keeps whichever line it saw first and fails one of these two)

a BARE in-file call on line 68 — `reportTwice n = describeTwice (twice n)`, where BOTH callees are module-level functions declared in this file. This is the lane's DEFAULT evidence tier, `usage_contextual`: the target is a known binding identified by its name rather than by a qualified spelling. Every other `calls` row across the eight Clean fixtures is qualified (`M.lookupOne`, `describe.nonNegative`, `withLocals.helper`, `Data.Error.Ok`), so before this pair the default tier was unpinned and a mutant that classified every `calls` edge reference_qualified would have passed. `describeTwice` is defined BELOW its use, which is the forward-reference case.

a BARE in-file call on line 68 — `reportTwice n = describeTwice (twice n)`, where BOTH callees are module-level functions declared in this file. This is the lane's DEFAULT evidence tier, `usage_contextual`: the target is a known binding identified by its name rather than by a qualified spelling. Every other `calls` row across the eight Clean fixtures is qualified (`M.lookupOne`, `describe.nonNegative`, `withLocals.helper`, `Data.Error.Ok`), so before this pair the default tier was unpinned and a mutant that classified every `calls` edge reference_qualified would have passed. `twice` is defined ABOVE its use. Two calls on one line, so both rows carry line 68 — the per-site line rule (M59.O2) and the name-keyed dedupe are different mechanisms and both apply.

forbidRelationships.comment: a HEAD pattern is not a body construction
a record literal is not a constructor application
no self-edge: the qualified call is the whole edge

the FP pin, stated positively: a pattern VARIABLE is not a field, so no `uses` edge is fabricated for it. `unwrap (Just v) = v` binds `v` and reads it; neither is a record field and neither produces an edge.
a field name is not a constructor
a parameter name is not a type reference
a LAMBDA parameter is not a generic: `twice = \k -> k + k` binds `k` and names no type

expectRelationshipCount.comment: the TYPE, exactly once. It was 2 when the container shared the name; the per-site rule now shows up as two DIFFERENT targets (this row and the `Point::instance` row) rather than as one name twice.
the instance container, exactly once, at the `instance Shape Point where` line
the two `!Int` domain types are ONE name, so they are one edge — dedupe is by source|type|target|line, and both domain types are on the signature's line

expectMetadata.comment: THE COMPLEXITY PAYLOAD, pinned as FILE metadata because that is where clean computes it: `ctx.fileComplexity` is the whole-file decision count and the analyzer stamps it as both `metadata.complexity` and `metadata.cyclomaticComplexity` (real-clean-analyzer.ts:885-887). 18 is measured on THIS fixture (the expression/declaration shapes fixture: 18 decision sites, 21 symbols) — the CLJ1 precedent, where a metadata pin is the only instrument that can hold a complexity baseline. A mutant that drops a branch construct drops the number and fails here.
